title: Retained Customers: Ordered in Both Month 1 and Month 2
description:
Find customers who placed an order in **January 2026 AND also in February 2026** (retained customers). Use set intersection of the two customer-id sets.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`, `city`, `country`

Output column: `name`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com','Chicago','USA'),(4,'Dan','dan@example.com','Mumbai','India'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-10','completed',100.00),(2,2,DATE '2026-01-20','completed',200.00),(3,1,DATE '2026-02-05','completed',150.00),(4,3,DATE '2026-02-15','completed',300.00),(5,2,DATE '2026-03-01','completed',250.00);
solution_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2026 AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 1 INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2026 AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 2) ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: Only Alice ordered in both January and February

hints: Build two SELECT lists: customer_ids who ordered in January, and those who ordered in February.
`INTERSECT` returns ids that appear in both result sets. Wrap it in `WHERE id IN (...)` to get names.
explanation: Jan orderers: Alice, Bob. Feb orderers: Alice, Carol. `INTERSECT` keeps only ids in both sets — Alice. Bob ordered in Jan and March, not Feb. Carol ordered in Feb but not Jan.
